benefits.title: Students gain more consistent access to meaningful experiential learning within their course
benefits.statement: King's can identify where curriculum-embedded experiential learning is limited, uneven or inaccessible and target change where it will make the greatest difference. This increases the likelihood that students can encounter meaningful opportunities to apply knowledge, exercise judgement, collaborate and engage with authentic contexts as part of their formal studies rather than relying on discretionary activity outside the curriculum.
benefits.benefitType: equitable curriculum access and educational development
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority gaps identified through curriculum review are acted on, students in targeted programmes encounter stronger and better-supported experiential learning, and access becomes less dependent on local history or individual academic champions.

benefits.title: Course teams can strengthen experiential learning with clearer evidence and practical support
benefits.statement: Programme and faculty teams gain a clearer view of existing strengths, hidden practice and gaps, alongside shared design and assurance expectations and access to targeted implementation support. This allows proportionate enhancement rather than requiring every team to diagnose the problem and invent the response from first principles.
benefits.beneficiary: Course teams, programme leaders, faculties and curriculum-support staff
benefits.benefitType: curriculum enhancement capability and effective use of academic effort
benefits.successLooksLike: Course teams can identify where experiential learning should be strengthened, draw on reusable approaches and specialist support, and implement change with clearer expectations around learning design, inclusion, reflection, assessment and evidence.

benefits.title: The University can target curriculum investment and assure growth more intelligently
benefits.statement: King's gains a repeatable evidence-to-action cycle linking curriculum review, the experiential-learning North Star, targeted investment and implementation evidence. This provides a stronger basis for deciding what to fund, where to scale successful models and where further support or assurance is needed.
benefits.benefitType: institutional assurance, prioritisation and investment effectiveness
benefits.successLooksLike: Curriculum growth decisions are traceable to evidence of need and educational purpose; funded interventions are reviewed for reach, quality and usefulness; and later investment is recalibrated using implementation evidence rather than carried forward automatically.
